# A mount callback failure strands later update requests

## Context

A bounded stability audit alongside #19477 found an earlier initialization path that never reaches common VDOM settlement. The operator prioritizes reproduced stability failures ahead of speculative hot-path optimization.

A real Component/Helper probe with the standard unit runtime produces the same result with current code and with the exact `08f43d63` public callback-dispatch methods restored in isolation. `initVnode` and `Abstract.afterSetMounted` are unchanged from that revision. This is an injected exception witness, not an observed application outage.

## The Problem

Register a resolver before `fresh.initVnode(true)`. In that resolver, mutate the component's VDOM, call `late = fresh.promiseUpdate()`, and throw.

Observed before fixture cleanup:
- Initial mount rejects with the injected error.
- `late` remains pending/unclaimed; `needsVdomUpdate` is true and the vnode still contains the earlier text.
- There is no in-flight entry, watchdog or post-update waiter.
- Both `updateBatch` and `resolveVdomUpdate` were called zero times. Destruction during fixture cleanup finally rejects `late`; the implementation did not recover it.

Design authority: the existing `promiseUpdate` failure contract must not strand parked requests. The accepted not-yet-mounted success exception remains binding; #18802 is NOT_PLANNED and must not be revived by this repair.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/component/Abstract.mjs#afterSetMounted` claims and dispatches mount callbacks before common settlement.
- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs#initVnode` catches the synchronous callback exception, clears flight/initialization flags and releases post-update work, but leaves this new request parked with no scheduled render.
- #19477 repairs the later `resolveVdomUpdate` boundary. Its initialization test covers a pre-update hook reached through that method, not this earlier mount callback.
- Existing `PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs` controls preserve first-render and unmounted-child settlement; owning initialization/lifecycle specs can hold the failure witness.

## The Fix

Repair exception cleanup at the existing initial-mount callback/initialization boundary. Settle requests covered by the failed attempt honestly and preserve or schedule their pending render work without clearing a distinct newer flight. Reuse existing lifecycle and callback ownership primitives. Keep the success-path mount exception unchanged; do not introduce a new rendering service or broad per-frame tracking.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Required behavior | Failure | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial mount failure | Existing `initVnode` cleanup and `promiseUpdate` contract | No stranded request or unscheduled dirty state | Reject affected requests; preserve separate newer work | Owning lifecycle JSDoc | Throwing mount resolver + late request |
| First-render success | Accepted #18802 disposition / #8082 behavior | Existing unmounted requests still settle at mount | No regression to await-mount callers | Existing promise JSDoc | Current first-render and unmounted-child controls |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The real-instance failure sequence reproduces before repair and afterwards leaves no permanently pending affected request.
- [ ] Queued rendering recovers or remains explicitly retryable under the existing failure contract; no silent dirty state with no execution path.
- [ ] Newer same-instance and reused-ID work survives old-attempt cleanup.
- [ ] Existing first-render and unmounted-child success controls remain unchanged and pass.
- [ ] Source/unit evidence stays distinct from any subsequently observed browser symptom.

## Out of Scope

Reversing #18802's success-path decision, sparse batching/depth policy, Main DOM deduplication, and assigning this pre-existing path to the #19468 regression.

Decision Record impact: none; restores failure liveness while retaining the accepted mount exception. Structure map: N/A; existing Body lifecycle owners, no new module.

### @neo-gpt-sophie - 2026-10-08T11:01:45Z

Next-step intake: the failure is at the initial-mount owner, before common settlement.

`initVnode()` sets `isVdomUpdating=true` and registers the initial full-depth flight before `Helper.create()`. `afterSetMounted()` then claims and dispatches mount callbacks. A callback's `promiseUpdate()` therefore parks as later work; when that callback throws, the initializer catch clears the initial flight but leaves that parked request and dirty state behind.

The next falsifier is a permanent real-component test for that sequence, paired with the existing first-render/unmounted-child success controls. The repair should make this initial failure cleanup settle the affected late request and preserve a subsequent render path, with instance checks protecting a replacement. It must retain #18802's accepted await-mount behavior. No implementation change is included in #19479.

The isolated older-callback control and current probe both recorded zero common-settlement calls and zero update batches, so this is independently useful work rather than another claim against the completed common-settlement repair.

Origin Session ID: e6ce4d70-a7ff-454e-996d-e7c25efdf4cf

### @neo-gpt-sophie - 2026-10-09T05:26:47Z

The permanent real-component tests reproduce the stranded request before repair. The current candidate repairs the initial failure boundary and keeps the accepted first-mount success exception.

The added controls cover: late work from a throwing mount resolver; a new flight and new phase work started during rejection; a reused-ID replacement; an overlapping initialization on the same instance; and old post-update waiters when rejection starts a retry. The last two controls caught weaknesses in the intermediate repair and now pass.

Failure cleanup is admitted only for the owning initialization attempt and current component instance. It detaches that attempt's post-update queue before callbacks, retires its flight, rejects parked own requests, releases captured waiters, and schedules dirty work only if another flight has not started. A private per-initialization token protects an overlapping retry; it is removed when its attempt ends. The ordinary update/settlement path is unchanged.

Validation: **38 focused tests passed; 4,871 full units passed, 2 skipped; 6/6 WorkstationBoot browser controls passed.** The error witnesses use real Component/Helper objects in the unit runtime; the browser controls witness preserved success behavior, not an observed application outage. No extra rendering service or per-frame generation map was introduced.
